lines.trans: Who are you hiding from right here, Max?
I am not hiding from anyone at all.
Chef just gave me urgent work.
I need to urgently check the electricity here.
And why do you have to be the one to do that?
Because I studied to be an electrician in Voronezh.
Alright then, go ahead and fix it in front of me.

examples.trans: What made you think that she likes me?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый').

examples.text: Здесь всегда продукты самого высокого качества.
examples.trans: There are always products of the highest quality here.

examples.text: Посмотрим, что тут самое безобидное.
examples.trans: Let us see what looks the most harmless in here.

examples.text: Да, это самый настоящий горячий плов.
examples.trans: Yes, this is real hot pilaf.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'без-' ('without, -less') (stem 'обидный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('harmless').

examples.text: Посмотрим, что тут самое безобидное.
examples.trans: Let us see what looks the most harmless in here.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень безобидный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very harmless choice.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'wow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Здесь всегда продукты самого высокого качества.
examples.trans: There are always products of the highest quality here.

examples.text: В зале сегодня очень много заказов.
examples.trans: There are very many orders in the dining room today.

examples.text: Сегодня у нас банкет для важного человека.
examples.trans: Today we have a banquet for an important man.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш ресторан всегда остаётся лучшим в Москве.
examples.trans: Our restaurant always remains the best in Moscow.

examples.text: У нас работает команда профессиональных поваров.
examples.trans: A team of professional chefs works here.

examples.text: У нас обслуживание гостей на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: Our guest service is at the highest level.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'whole', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Представь, унесли вообще весь сейф.
examples.trans: Imagine, they carried off the entire safe.

examples.text: Там все дома радуются и весело смеются.
examples.trans: Everyone at home rejoices and laughs merrily there.

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И третье — это любые твои шутки.
examples.trans: And third, any of your jokes.

examples.text: У вас ужасное чувство юмора, Максим.
examples.trans: You have a terrible sense of humor, Maxim.

examples.text: Мне надо срочно проверить тут электричество.
examples.trans: I need to urgently check the electricity here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Макс, ты к нам на свадьбу один придёшь?
examples.trans: Max, will you come to our wedding alone?

examples.text: По всем признакам всё сходится.
examples.trans: By all the signs, everything adds up.

examples.text: По признакам всё точно сходится.
examples.trans: By the signs, everything matches up.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'охранитель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'fuse' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Один предохранитель живой, сейчас остальные проверим.
examples.trans: One fuse is alive, now we will check the others.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть предохранитель.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always fuse.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('alive').

examples.text: У нас обслуживание гостей на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: Our guest service is at the highest level.

examples.text: Один предохранитель живой, сейчас остальные проверим.
examples.trans: One fuse is alive, now we will check the others.

examples.text: Макс, скажи, ты там вообще живой?
examples.trans: Max, tell me, are you even alive over there?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('remaining, other').

examples.text: Один предохранитель живой, сейчас остальные проверим.
examples.trans: One fuse is alive, now we will check the others.

examples.text: А остальное — это уже не наши проблемы.
examples.trans: And the rest is no longer our problem.

examples.text: А где остальные детишки?
examples.trans: And where are the rest of the children?
